instruction:
# Multi-User Todo Application Database Schema

## User Account & Authentication
- Users table with: id (UUID, primary key), email (unique, lowercase, indexed), password_hash (hashed with bcrypt), created_at, updated_at

## User Profile
- Profiles table with: id (UUID, primary key, same as user id, foreign key to users), display_name (required, max 100 characters), updated_at
- One-to-one relationship: User <-> Profile

## Todos
- Todos table with:
  - id (UUID, primary key)
  - user_id (UUID, foreign key to users, cascade delete on account deletion)
  - title (string, required, max 255 characters)
  - description (text, optional, can be empty)
  - start_date (date, optional)
  - due_date (date, optional)
  - is_complete (boolean, default false)
  - is_deleted (boolean, default false, for soft delete)
  - deleted_at (timestamp, null if not deleted)
  - created_at (timestamp)
  - updated_at (timestamp)
- Index on user_id, is_complete, is_deleted, created_at, start_date, due_date

## Edit History
- TodoEdits table with:
  - id (UUID, primary key)
  - todo_id (UUID, foreign key to todos, cascade delete)
  - edited_at (timestamp)
  - old_title (string, nullable)
  - new_title (string, nullable)
  - old_description (text, nullable)
  - new_description (text, nullable)
  - old_start_date (date, nullable)
  - new_start_date (date, nullable)
  - old_due_date (date, nullable)
  - new_due_date (date, nullable)
- Index on todo_id, edited_at (descending)

## Business Rules
- A user's todos are private - users can only access their own todos
- When user account is deleted, all their todos (including deleted ones in trash) are permanently deleted
- When a todo is soft deleted, is_deleted becomes true and deleted_at is set
- When a todo is permanently deleted from trash, its edit history is also deleted
- When restoring a todo from trash, is_deleted becomes false and deleted_at becomes null
- Edit history is created only when at least one field changes during an update
- todos.sort_start_date: todos without start_date appear at end
- todos.sort_due_date: todos without due_date appear at end
- Edit history entries sorted from most recent to oldest

models.name: multi_user_todo_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts identified by device fingerprint for unauthenticated access.

This table stores guest user sessions that allow unauthenticated visitors to access the system without creating a full member account. Each guest is uniquely identified by a device fingerprint combination.

Guest accounts are temporary and may be cleaned up periodically. They enable basic functionality for users who have not yet registered or logged in.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the guest account.

plainFields.name: fingerprint_hash
plainFields.description:
Hashed device fingerprint used to uniquely identify guest sessions.

Combined from user agent, IP address, and browser characteristics to create a persistent identifier for unauthenticated users.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser user agent string captured at session creation.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: Client IP address captured at session creation.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Current status of the guest session.

Values: active, expired, deleted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this guest account.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted.

models.name: multi_user_todo_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest access without full authentication.

Maintains audit trail of guest device and access information with explicit expiration. Each session belongs to exactly one guest account and is managed through the guest's lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_guest_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the guest account that owns this session.

Each session belongs to exactly one guest and is deleted when the guest account is deleted (cascade delete).

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the device that created this session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page where the guest session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL from the guest's browser, indicating how they arrived at the site.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for this session. Sessions become invalid after this time.

models.name: multi_user_todo_members
models.description:
Registered member accounts with email and password authentication credentials for the multi-user todo application.

## Identity and Authentication

Stores user login credentials including unique email address and bcrypt-hashed password. Used exclusively for member actor authentication and authorization.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
Unique email address for user authentication and identification.

Must be lowercase, unique across all accounts, and used as the primary login identifier.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description:
Bcrypt-hashed password for secure authentication.

Never stored in plaintext. Updated when user changes password during account management flows.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null when account is active, set when account is deleted to mark for permanent removal.

models.name: multi_user_todo_member_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh token support.

Stores active login sessions for authenticated members. Each session is associated with exactly one member account and includes client context (IP, referrer, last URL). Sessions expire automatically and are cascaded when the member account is deleted.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the member account that owns this session.

Establishes a 1:N relationship where each session belongs to exactly one member. When the member account is deleted, all associated sessions are automatically deleted (cascade). This ensures orphaned sessions are never created or left behind when accounts are removed.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description:
Client IP address when the session was created.

Used for security auditing and detecting suspicious login activity from different locations.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description:
Last visited URL path when the session was active.

Provides context about which page the member was viewing when the session token was generated or last used.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description:
HTTP Referrer header value when the session was created.

Indicates which page or external site the member came from when logging in or creating the session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the session was first created.

Records the exact moment the member logged in and the session token was issued.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the session expires and becomes invalid.

Used for automatic session cleanup and security. Sessions must be refreshed or re-authenticated before this time.

models.name: multi_user_todo_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for member account recovery, providing secure temporary access to reset forgotten passwords.

This table stores one-time use tokens that members receive via email after requesting a password reset. Each token is tied to a specific member account and expires after a predetermined time period for security. Once a token is used to reset a password, it is immediately invalidated and marked for deletion.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description:
References the member account requesting the password reset.

This foreign key ensures each reset token is associated with exactly one member account. The relationship is 1:1 - a member can have at most one active password reset token at any time. When the member account is deleted, all associated reset tokens are cascaded and deleted.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description:
Unique secure token string for password reset.

A cryptographically random token (at least 32 characters, typically 64+ characters using random string generation) that is sent to the member's registered email address. The member includes this token in the password reset form submission. Tokens are single-use only - once a token is successfully used, it is immediately invalidated and cannot be reused.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this password reset token expires.

The token becomes invalid after this datetime passes. Tokens typically expire after 1-24 hours depending on security policy. The system must reject any token whose expired_at timestamp is in the past, even if the token has not been used yet. This prevents long-term security risks from compromised or leaked tokens.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this password reset token was created.

Used to track token age and enforce expiration policy. The difference between created_at and current time should not exceed the allowed token lifetime window.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this password reset token was last updated.

For token tables, this field is typically not updated after creation as tokens should be immutable until deletion. However, it is included here to maintain consistency with the temporal field pattern used across all business entity tables.

models.name: multi_user_todo_member_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for registration confirmation and validation.

Each token is a one-time use code that expires after a short period to prevent unauthorized verification. Tokens are created during registration and must be validated before the user account becomes fully active.

Relationships:
- Belongs to exactly one {@link multi_user_todo_members} through member_id foreign key
- Tokens are invalidated after verification or expiration

Indexes optimize lookup by email, member, and expiration for security token cleanup.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description:
References the member account associated with this email verification token.

Each email verification is tied to exactly one member account. The token is used to verify ownership of the email address associated with that member.

Deleted at cascade: When a member account is deleted, all associated email verification tokens are permanently removed to maintain data integrity and prevent orphaned records.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description:
Unique verification token used to confirm email ownership during registration.

This is a secure, randomly generated string that must be submitted to verify the email address. Each token can only be used once for verification.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
Email address being verified during the registration process.

This matches the email address provided when creating the member account. Used as a reference to identify which email is being verified.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this verification token expires.

Tokens are short-lived for security purposes. Expired tokens cannot be used for verification and will be periodically cleaned up by the system to prevent accumulation of stale tokens.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this verification token was created.

Used to determine token age and for audit trail purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this verification token record was last updated.

Used to track when verification attempts or token refreshes occur.

models.name: multi_user_todo_todos
models.description:
Main todo entity with lifecycle tracking including completion status, soft delete, and date fields.

Business entities representing individual tasks or to-do items that users can create and manage. Each todo belongs to exactly one member user and can track its completion state, soft deletion status, and optional date fields for scheduling.

Lifecycle Management: Todos support a soft-delete pattern where deleted todos move to trash (is_deleted=true, deleted_at set). They can be restored from trash (is_deleted=false, deleted_at=null) or permanently deleted. Completion status is tracked with is_complete boolean flag that can be toggled.

Date Fields: Optional start_date and due_date fields enable basic scheduling and filtering. Todos without start_date appear at the end when sorted by start_date. Todos without due_date appear at the end when sorted by due_date.

Data Ownership: Each todo is owned by exactly one member user and is private - users can only access their own todos.

See {@link multi_user_todo_member_sessions} for session management, {@link multi_user_todo_todos_edits} for edit history audit trail.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key identifier for the todo.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description:
References the member user who owns this todo.

Cascade delete ensures all todos are removed when a member account is deleted. Users can only access their own todos through this foreign key relationship.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description:
Todo title or name.

Required field with a maximum length of 255 characters to ensure concise task identification. This is the primary identifier shown in todo lists.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Optional todo description or additional details.

Can be empty or null if no additional context is provided. Supports flexible todo item definitions.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description:
Optional start date when the todo begins.

When sorting by start_date, todos without a start date appear at the end of the list. Enables basic task scheduling and chronological organization.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description:
Optional due date when the todo should be completed.

When sorting by due_date, todos without a due date appear at the end of the list. Enables deadline tracking and priority management.

plainFields.name: is_complete
plainFields.description:
Completion status flag for the todo.

Defaults to false when created. Can be toggled to true when the todo is finished. Users can mark todos as complete or return them to incomplete status.

plainFields.name: is_deleted
plainFields.description:
Soft delete flag indicating trash status.

Defaults to false. When true, the todo is in trash but not permanently deleted. Enables trash functionality for accidental deletion recovery.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the todo was soft deleted to trash.

Null when the todo is active. Set to current time when is_deleted becomes true. Can be cleared (set to null) when restoring from trash.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the todo was created.

Always set to the current time on create. Used for ordering and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the todo was last updated.

Always set to the current time on create and each update. Enables tracking of most recently modified todos.

models.name: multi_user_todo_todos_edits
models.description:
Audit trail table recording all field changes to todos including old and new values for title, description, and date fields.

This table provides an immutable history of todo modifications, capturing what values existed before and after each edit. Each edit record is created only when at least one field actually changes during a todo update operation.

foreignFields.name: todo_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the todo that was edited.

When the referenced todo is permanently deleted, this edit record is cascade deleted to maintain referential integrity.

plainFields.name: edited_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was last edited. Used for sorting edit history from most recent to oldest.

plainFields.name: old_title
plainFields.description: The todo title value before the edit. Null if title was not part of this edit.

plainFields.name: new_title
plainFields.description: The todo title value after the edit. Null if title was not part of this edit.

plainFields.name: old_description
plainFields.description: The todo description value before the edit. Null if description was not part of this edit.

plainFields.name: new_description
plainFields.description: The todo description value after the edit. Null if description was not part of this edit.

plainFields.name: old_start_date
plainFields.description: The todo start_date value before the edit. Null if start_date was not part of this edit.

plainFields.name: new_start_date
plainFields.description: The todo start_date value after the edit. Null if start_date was not part of this edit.

plainFields.name: old_due_date
plainFields.description: The todo due_date value before the edit. Null if due_date was not part of this edit.

plainFields.name: new_due_date
plainFields.description: The todo due_date value after the edit. Null if due_date was not part of this edit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this edit record was created. Automatically set on insert.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this edit record was last updated. Always matches created_at for append-only edit records.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this edit record was soft deleted. Null if not deleted. Used for soft delete support.

### `multi_user_todo_guests`

Temporary guest accounts identified by device fingerprint for
unauthenticated access.

This table stores guest user sessions that allow unauthenticated visitors
to access the system without creating a full member account. Each guest
is uniquely identified by a device fingerprint combination.

Guest accounts are temporary and may be cleaned up periodically. They
enable basic functionality for users who have not yet registered or
logged in.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key for the guest account.
- `fingerprint_hash`
  > Hashed device fingerprint used to uniquely identify guest sessions.
  >
  > Combined from user agent, IP address, and browser characteristics to
  > create a persistent identifier for unauthenticated users.
- `user_agent`: Browser user agent string captured at session creation.
- `ip_address`: Client IP address captured at session creation.
- `status`
  > Current status of the guest session.
  >
  > Values: active, expired, deleted.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the guest account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last update to this guest account.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted.

### `multi_user_todo_guest_sessions`

Temporary session tokens for guest access without full authentication.

Maintains audit trail of guest device and access information with
explicit expiration. Each session belongs to exactly one guest account
and is managed through the guest's lifecycle.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `multi_user_todo_guest_id`
  > Reference to the guest account that owns this session.
  >
  > Each session belongs to exactly one guest and is deleted when the guest
  > account is deleted (cascade delete).
- `ip`: IP address of the device that created this session.
- `href`: URL of the page where the guest session was initiated.
- `referrer`
  > Referrer URL from the guest's browser, indicating how they arrived at the
  > site.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this session was created.
- `expired_at`
  > Expiration timestamp for this session. Sessions become invalid after this
  > time.

### `multi_user_todo_members`

Registered member accounts with email and password authentication
credentials for the multi-user todo application.

## Identity and Authentication

Stores user login credentials including unique email address and
bcrypt-hashed password. Used exclusively for member actor authentication
and authorization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Unique email address for user authentication and identification.
  >
  > Must be lowercase, unique across all accounts, and used as the primary
  > login identifier.
- `password_hash`
  > Bcrypt-hashed password for secure authentication.
  >
  > Never stored in plaintext. Updated when user changes password during
  > account management flows.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the member account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp. Null when account is active, set when account is
  > deleted to mark for permanent removal.

### `multi_user_todo_member_sessions`

JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh
token support.

Stores active login sessions for authenticated members. Each session is
associated with exactly one member account and includes client context
(IP, referrer, last URL). Sessions expire automatically and are cascaded
when the member account is deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `multi_user_todo_member_id`
  > Foreign key reference to the member account that owns this session.
  >
  > Establishes a 1:N relationship where each session belongs to exactly one
  > member. When the member account is deleted, all associated sessions are
  > automatically deleted (cascade). This ensures orphaned sessions are never
  > created or left behind when accounts are removed.
- `ip`
  > Client IP address when the session was created.
  >
  > Used for security auditing and detecting suspicious login activity from
  > different locations.
- `href`
  > Last visited URL path when the session was active.
  >
  > Provides context about which page the member was viewing when the session
  > token was generated or last used.
- `referrer`
  > HTTP Referrer header value when the session was created.
  >
  > Indicates which page or external site the member came from when logging
  > in or creating the session.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the session was first created.
  >
  > Records the exact moment the member logged in and the session token was
  > issued.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when the session expires and becomes invalid.
  >
  > Used for automatic session cleanup and security. Sessions must be
  > refreshed or re-authenticated before this time.

### `multi_user_todo_member_password_resets`

Password reset tokens for member account recovery, providing secure
temporary access to reset forgotten passwords.

This table stores one-time use tokens that members receive via email
after requesting a password reset. Each token is tied to a specific
member account and expires after a predetermined time period for
security. Once a token is used to reset a password, it is immediately
invalidated and marked for deletion.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `member_id`
  > References the member account requesting the password reset.
  >
  > This foreign key ensures each reset token is associated with exactly one
  > member account. The relationship is 1:1 - a member can have at most one
  > active password reset token at any time. When the member account is
  > deleted, all associated reset tokens are cascaded and deleted.
- `token`
  > Unique secure token string for password reset.
  >
  > A cryptographically random token (at least 32 characters, typically 64+
  > characters using random string generation) that is sent to the member's
  > registered email address. The member includes this token in the password
  > reset form submission. Tokens are single-use only - once a token is
  > successfully used, it is immediately invalidated and cannot be reused.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when this password reset token expires.
  >
  > The token becomes invalid after this datetime passes. Tokens typically
  > expire after 1-24 hours depending on security policy. The system must
  > reject any token whose expired_at timestamp is in the past, even if the
  > token has not been used yet. This prevents long-term security risks from
  > compromised or leaked tokens.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this password reset token was created.
  >
  > Used to track token age and enforce expiration policy. The difference
  > between created_at and current time should not exceed the allowed token
  > lifetime window.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this password reset token was last updated.
  >
  > For token tables, this field is typically not updated after creation as
  > tokens should be immutable until deletion. However, it is included here
  > to maintain consistency with the temporal field pattern used across all
  > business entity tables.

### `multi_user_todo_member_email_verifications`

Email verification tokens for registration confirmation and validation.

Each token is a one-time use code that expires after a short period to
prevent unauthorized verification. Tokens are created during registration
and must be validated before the user account becomes fully active.

Relationships:
- Belongs to exactly one [multi_user_todo_members](#multi_user_todo_members) through
member_id foreign key
- Tokens are invalidated after verification or expiration

Indexes optimize lookup by email, member, and expiration for security
token cleanup.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `member_id`
  > References the member account associated with this email verification
  > token.
  >
  > Each email verification is tied to exactly one member account. The token
  > is used to verify ownership of the email address associated with that
  > member.
  >
  > Deleted at cascade: When a member account is deleted, all associated
  > email verification tokens are permanently removed to maintain data
  > integrity and prevent orphaned records.
- `token`
  > Unique verification token used to confirm email ownership during
  > registration.
  >
  > This is a secure, randomly generated string that must be submitted to
  > verify the email address. Each token can only be used once for
  > verification.
- `email`
  > Email address being verified during the registration process.
  >
  > This matches the email address provided when creating the member account.
  > Used as a reference to identify which email is being verified.
- `expires_at`
  > Timestamp when this verification token expires.
  >
  > Tokens are short-lived for security purposes. Expired tokens cannot be
  > used for verification and will be periodically cleaned up by the system
  > to prevent accumulation of stale tokens.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this verification token was created.
  >
  > Used to determine token age and for audit trail purposes.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this verification token record was last updated.
  >
  > Used to track when verification attempts or token refreshes occur.

### `multi_user_todo_todos`

Main todo entity with lifecycle tracking including completion status,
soft delete, and date fields.

Business entities representing individual tasks or to-do items that users
can create and manage. Each todo belongs to exactly one member user and
can track its completion state, soft deletion status, and optional date
fields for scheduling.

Lifecycle Management: Todos support a soft-delete pattern where deleted
todos move to trash (is_deleted=true, deleted_at set). They can be
restored from trash (is_deleted=false, deleted_at=null) or permanently
deleted. Completion status is tracked with is_complete boolean flag that
can be toggled.

Date Fields: Optional start_date and due_date fields enable basic
scheduling and filtering. Todos without start_date appear at the end when
sorted by start_date. Todos without due_date appear at the end when
sorted by due_date.

Data Ownership: Each todo is owned by exactly one member user and is
private - users can only access their own todos.

See [multi_user_todo_member_sessions](#multi_user_todo_member_sessions) for session management,
[multi_user_todo_todos_edits](#multi_user_todo_todos_edits) for edit history audit trail.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key identifier for the todo.
- `multi_user_todo_member_id`
  > References the member user who owns this todo.
  >
  > Cascade delete ensures all todos are removed when a member account is
  > deleted. Users can only access their own todos through this foreign key
  > relationship.
- `title`
  > Todo title or name.
  >
  > Required field with a maximum length of 255 characters to ensure concise
  > task identification. This is the primary identifier shown in todo lists.
- `description`
  > Optional todo description or additional details.
  >
  > Can be empty or null if no additional context is provided. Supports
  > flexible todo item definitions.
- `start_date`
  > Optional start date when the todo begins.
  >
  > When sorting by start_date, todos without a start date appear at the end
  > of the list. Enables basic task scheduling and chronological
  > organization.
- `due_date`
  > Optional due date when the todo should be completed.
  >
  > When sorting by due_date, todos without a due date appear at the end of
  > the list. Enables deadline tracking and priority management.
- `is_complete`
  > Completion status flag for the todo.
  >
  > Defaults to false when created. Can be toggled to true when the todo is
  > finished. Users can mark todos as complete or return them to incomplete
  > status.
- `is_deleted`
  > Soft delete flag indicating trash status.
  >
  > Defaults to false. When true, the todo is in trash but not permanently
  > deleted. Enables trash functionality for accidental deletion recovery.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was soft deleted to trash.
  >
  > Null when the todo is active. Set to current time when is_deleted becomes
  > true. Can be cleared (set to null) when restoring from trash.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was created.
  >
  > Always set to the current time on create. Used for ordering and audit
  > purposes.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was last updated.
  >
  > Always set to the current time on create and each update. Enables
  > tracking of most recently modified todos.

### `multi_user_todo_todos_edits`

Audit trail table recording all field changes to todos including old and
new values for title, description, and date fields.

This table provides an immutable history of todo modifications, capturing
what values existed before and after each edit. Each edit record is
created only when at least one field actually changes during a todo
update operation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_id`
  > Foreign key reference to the todo that was edited.
  >
  > When the referenced todo is permanently deleted, this edit record is
  > cascade deleted to maintain referential integrity.
- `edited_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was last edited. Used for sorting edit history
  > from most recent to oldest.
- `old_title`
  > The todo title value before the edit. Null if title was not part of this
  > edit.
- `new_title`
  > The todo title value after the edit. Null if title was not part of this
  > edit.
- `old_description`
  > The todo description value before the edit. Null if description was not
  > part of this edit.
- `new_description`
  > The todo description value after the edit. Null if description was not
  > part of this edit.
- `old_start_date`
  > The todo start_date value before the edit. Null if start_date was not
  > part of this edit.
- `new_start_date`
  > The todo start_date value after the edit. Null if start_date was not part
  > of this edit.
- `old_due_date`
  > The todo due_date value before the edit. Null if due_date was not part of
  > this edit.
- `new_due_date`
  > The todo due_date value after the edit. Null if due_date was not part of
  > this edit.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this edit record was created. Automatically set on insert.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this edit record was last updated. Always matches
  > created_at for append-only edit records.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this edit record was soft deleted. Null if not deleted.
  > Used for soft delete support.

# Multi-User Todo Application API Specification

## Authentication Endpoints

### POST /auth/signup
Create a new user account with email and password.
- Request body:
  - email: string, required, valid email format, unique
  - password: string, required, minimum 8 characters
- Response: 201 Created with user id and email
- Error: 400 Bad Request for validation errors, 409 Conflict if email exists

### POST /auth/login
Authenticate user and return session token.
- Request body:
  - email: string, required, valid email format
  - password: string, required
- Response: 200 OK with access_token and refresh_token
- Error: 401 Unauthorized for invalid credentials

### POST /auth/password
Change user's password.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Request body:
  - current_password: string, required
  - new_password: string, required, minimum 8 characters
- Response: 200 OK with success message
- Error: 400 Bad Request for validation errors, 401 Unauthorized for wrong current password

### DELETE /auth/account
Delete user account and all associated data.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Response: 200 OK with success message
- Note: Permanently deletes all user's todos (including trash) and edit history

## User Profile Endpoints

### GET /profile
Get current user's profile information.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Response: 200 OK with display_name, email, created_at
- Note: Users cannot view other users' profiles

### PUT /profile
Update user's display name.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Request body:
  - display_name: string, required, max 100 characters
- Response: 200 OK with updated profile
- Error: 400 Bad Request for validation errors

## Todo Endpoints

### GET /todos
List user's todos with pagination, filtering, and sorting.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Query parameters:
  - page: integer, optional, default 1, minimum 1
  - limit: integer, optional, default 20, maximum 100
  - status: string, optional, enum [all, complete, incomplete]
  - sortBy: string, optional, enum [created_at, start_date, due_date]
  - sortOrder: string, optional, enum [asc, desc]
- Response: 200 OK with paginated todos array and pagination metadata
  - Each todo: id, title, is_complete, start_date, due_date, created_at
  - Metadata: total_count, page, limit, total_pages

### GET /todos/:id
Get a single todo by ID with full details.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Response: 200 OK with complete todo object
- Error: 404 Not Found if todo doesn't exist or doesn't belong to user

### POST /todos
Create a new todo.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Request body:
  - title: string, required, max 255 characters
  - description: string, optional, max 10000 characters
  - start_date: string (ISO date), optional
  - due_date: string (ISO date), optional
- Response: 201 Created with created todo object
- Error: 400 Bad Request for validation errors

### PUT /todos/:id
Edit an existing todo. Creates an edit history entry.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Request body (all optional):
  - title: string, max 255 characters
  - description: string, max 10000 characters
  - start_date: string (ISO date), optional
  - due_date: string (ISO date), optional
- At least one field must be changed
- Response: 200 OK with updated todo
- Error: 400 Bad Request for validation errors, 404 Not Found if todo doesn't exist

### DELETE /todos/:id
Soft delete a todo (move to trash).
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Response: 200 OK with deleted todo
- Error: 400 Bad Request if already deleted, 404 Not Found

## Edit History Endpoints

### GET /todos/:id/history
Get edit history for a specific todo.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Response: 200 OK with array of edit history entries (sorted from most recent to oldest)
  - Each entry: id, edited_at, old_title, new_title, old_description, new_description, old_start_date, new_start_date, old_due_date, new_due_date
- Error: 404 Not Found if todo doesn't exist

## Trash Endpoints

### GET /trash
List user's deleted todos (trash) with pagination.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Query parameters:
  - page: integer, optional, default 1, minimum 1
  - limit: integer, optional, default 20, maximum 100
- Response: 200 OK with paginated deleted todos and metadata

### PUT /trash/:id/restore
Restore a todo from trash back to active list.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Response: 200 OK with restored todo
- Error: 400 Bad Request if not in trash, 404 Not Found

### DELETE /trash/:id
Permanently delete a todo from trash.
- Requires: Authentication header with access_token
- Response: 200 OK with success message
- Note: Also deletes all edit history for this todo
- Error: 404 Not Found if todo not in trash

## Authentication Middleware
All authenticated endpoints require a valid access_token in the Authorization header:
- Format: Bearer <token>
- Token is validated and user_id is extracted and attached to request context

## Response Format
All responses follow consistent format:
- Success: Standard HTTP status with response body
- Error: HTTP status code with error object containing:
  - error: string, error code
  - message: string, human-readable message
  - details: object, additional error details (optional)

operations.specification: Create a guest account with email and password. Validate email format and password minimum length. Create multi_user_todo_guests record with fingerprint_hash (from device fingerprint), user_agent, and ip_address. Create associated multi_user_todo_guest_sessions record with ip, created_at, expired_at (set to 1 hour from now). Generate JWT access token and refresh token. Return IMultiUserTodoGuest.IAuthorized with both tokens. Error handling: 400 for validation errors (invalid email format, password less than 8 characters), 409 Conflict if email already exists.
operations.description:
Create a new guest account with email and password.

Registers a new guest user with the provided email and password credentials. The system creates a temporary guest account identified by device fingerprint and stores associated session information for authentication purposes.

The endpoint validates the email format and ensures the password meets minimum security requirements (at least 8 characters). Upon successful creation, JWT access and refresh tokens are generated and returned for subsequent authenticated requests.

Security considerations: Device fingerprint (user_agent, ip_address) is stored to enable session tracking. Tokens have expiration times and must be refreshed before expiry. Password is hashed before storage.

requestBody.description: Guest account registration credentials

responseBody.description: Authorization tokens and guest account information

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Refresh existing access token using a valid refresh token. Validate the refresh token from the request body. If valid, generate new access token and refresh token pair. Update the session in multi_user_todo_guest_sessions table with new expired_at timestamp (1 hour from now). Return IMultiUserTodoGuest.IAuthorized with new tokens. Error handling: 401 Unauthorized if refresh token is invalid, expired, or malformed.
operations.description:
Renew an expired access token using a refresh token.

This endpoint allows guest users to obtain new JWT tokens without re-authenticating. The provided refresh token is validated against stored sessions in multi_user_todo_guest_sessions. Upon successful validation, new access and refresh tokens are generated.

The refresh token has a longer validity period than the access token and is used exclusively for token renewal. After successful refresh, the session's expired_at timestamp is updated to extend the session lifetime.

Security considerations: Only valid, non-expired refresh tokens can be used. Each refresh generates a new token pair, invalidating the previous refresh token. This prevents token replay attacks and maintains session security.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for token renewal

responseBody.description: New authorization tokens

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification:
Create a new member account with email and password.

1. Validate email format (valid email pattern)
2. Validate password length (minimum 8 characters)
3. Check if email already exists in multi_user_todo_members
4. Hash password using bcrypt
5. Insert new record into multi_user_todo_members with email, password_hash
6. Create initial session in multi_user_todo_member_sessions with:
   - member_id: newly created member id
   - ip: from request context or default
   - href: from request context or default
   - referrer: from request context or default
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - expired_at: access token expiry (e.g., 1 hour from now)
   - Note: refresh token also stored as part of session
7. Return access_token and refresh_token in response
8. Errors: 400 for validation errors, 409 for duplicate email
operations.description:
Register a new member account with email and password.

Creates a new member account in the multi_user_todo_members table after validating the email format and password requirements. The password is hashed using bcrypt before storage. Upon successful registration, an initial session is created and both access and refresh tokens are returned.

Validation ensures the email is in valid format, password is at least 8 characters, and the email is not already registered. Duplicate email addresses return a 409 Conflict error.

requestBody.description: Registration request containing email and password

responseBody.description: Authentication response containing access and refresh tokens

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
Authenticate member with email and password.

1. Validate email format
2. Find member in multi_user_todo_members by email
3. Verify password using bcrypt comparison
4. Check if member account is active (deleted_at is null)
5. Create new session in multi_user_todo_member_sessions:
   - member_id: member id

operations.description:
List all authentication sessions with pagination, filtering, and sorting options.

Returns paginated list of member sessions for security auditing and session management. Sessions include client context such as IP address, referrer, and last visited URL. The endpoint supports filtering by date ranges, expiration status, and sorting options to help identify active sessions, expired sessions, or sessions from specific time periods.

All sessions are owned by authenticated members. Users can only view their own sessions, not other members' sessions. Each session entry provides complete lifecycle information from creation to expiration.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_member_sessions table with pagination and filtering.

**Filtering Logic**:
- Apply optional member_id filter if provided (member can only filter their own sessions)
- Apply created_at range filter if start_date and/or end_date provided
- Apply expired_at range filter if provided
- Apply status filter: 'active' (expired_at > now), 'expired' (expired_at <= now), or 'all'

**Sorting Logic**:
- sortBy parameter: 'created_at', 'expired_at', or 'ip'
- sortOrder parameter: 'asc' or 'desc'
- Default sort: created_at descending

**Pagination Logic**:
- page: 1-indexed page number, default 1
- limit: items per page, default 20, max 100
- Calculate total_count for pagination metadata

**Implementation Details**:
- SELECT * FROM multi_user_todo_member_sessions
- Apply WHERE filters for member_id, date ranges, expiration status
- Apply ORDER BY with NULLS LAST for expired_at when sorting
- Apply LIMIT and OFFSET for pagination
- Count total rows for pagination metadata
- Return session objects

**Edge Cases**:
- No sessions match filters: return empty array with total_count = 0
- Invalid sort field: default to created_at
- Invalid sort order: default to desc
- Page out of range: return empty array or last page

operations.name: index

Query multi_user_todo_member_password_resets table with pagination and filtering.

1. Validate authentication - require active session with valid access_token
2. For member users: filter by member_id = current_user.id; for administrators: no member_id filter
3. Apply search filters:
   - member_id: exact match (optional)
   - status: 'valid' (not expired) or 'expired' based on expired_at comparison
   - date ranges: created_at >= and <=, expired_at >= and <=
   - member_id: filter by specific member
4. Join with multi_user_todo_members to get member.display_name
5. Sort by created_at DESC (most recent first)
6. Apply pagination: page, limit, calculate total_pages
7. Return only summary fields (exclude token for security)

- NEVER include actual token value in response
- Never expose other users' password reset requests
- Always validate member_id belongs to current user for non-admin users

- Empty result set: return empty array with pagination metadata showing 0 total
- Invalid date formats: reject with 400 Bad Request

This operation returns metadata about a specific password reset token, including its creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, the associated member account identifier, and token status information. The actual reset token value is never exposed through this endpoint for security reasons.

The endpoint is intended for administrative use cases such as:
- Auditing password reset activity for security compliance
- Troubleshooting password reset issues for support teams
- Monitoring token usage and expiration patterns
- Support investigations requiring token status verification

operations.specification:
Retrieve password reset token by UUID from multi_user_todo_member_password_resets table.

Query the table using resetId as the primary key to fetch the complete token record.

Perform the following validation checks in order:
1. Verify password reset token exists in database by UUID lookup
2. Check token is not expired (expired_at > current_time) - return status indicator
3. Verify token has not been used - tokens are cascaded when used (deleted from DB)
4. Verify requesting user has admin role in authentication context

Return the password reset token metadata without exposing the actual token string.

Calculate time_until_expiration_seconds as integer seconds difference between expired_at and current_time.

Perform join with multi_user_todo_members table using member_id foreign key to include:
- member.id as member_id
- member.email as member_email
- member.display_name as member_display_name

Return comprehensive token metadata for administrative review.

- Return 404 Not Found if password reset token not found by UUID
- Return 403 Forbidden if requesting user lacks admin privileges
- Return 401 Unauthorized if not authenticated or token validation failed
- Return 400 Bad Request if resetId is not a valid UUID format

Response includes status indicators: is_expired, is_valid, time_until_expiration_seconds.

Filtering supports three status categories: all todos, only complete todos, or only incomplete todos. Sorting can be applied to creation date, start date, or due date in ascending or descending order. Todos without date values appear at the end when sorted by those fields.

   - "all": No filter on is_complete
   - "complete": Filter where is_complete = true
   - "incomplete": Filter where is_complete = false

4. Sorting (if provided in request body):
   - created_at (default), start_date, or due_date
   - asc or desc order
   - NULL values for start_date/due_date appear at end in asc order

5. Pagination: Apply LIMIT and OFFSET based on page and limit parameters

6. Return: Todo summary fields (id, title, is_complete, start_date, due_date, created_at) with total_count and pagination metadata

7. Validation: page >= 1 (default 1), limit >= 1 and <= 100 (default 20), sortBy must be valid enum value (created_at/start_date/due_date), sortOrder must be valid enum value (asc/desc)

- Returns 400 Bad Request if the title is not provided or exceeds 255 characters
- Returns 400 Bad Request if the description exceeds 10,000 characters
- Returns 401 Unauthorized if the user is not authenticated
- Returns 409 Conflict if the email already exists during account creation (not applicable here)
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new todo record in the multi_user_todo_todos table.

1. Validate authentication - ensure the request contains a valid access_token belonging to a member user.
2. Parse the request body and validate:
   - title: required, string, max 255 characters, must be non-empty
   - description: optional, string, max 10000 characters, can be null or empty
   - start_date: optional, ISO 8601 date-time format
   - due_date: optional, ISO 8601 date-time format
3. Set is_complete to false (default)
4. Set is_deleted to false (default)
5. Set multi_user_todo_member_id to the authenticated user's ID
6. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
7. Set deleted_at to null (default)
8. Generate a new UUID for the id field
9. Insert the record into multi_user_todo_todos table
10. Return the created todo object with all fields populated

responseBody.description: The newly created todo object with all fields including the system-assigned ID, member association, completion status, timestamps, and any provided date fields.

requestBody.description: Todo creation data. Title is required and must be between 1 and 255 characters. Description is optional and can be up to 10,000 characters. Start date and due date are optional date-time values. If not provided, the todo will be marked as incomplete by default.

operations.description:
Update an existing todo record with new field values.

This endpoint allows users to modify any combination of todo fields (title, description, start_date, due_date). When at least one field changes, an edit history entry is automatically created to track the modification. The operation validates that the requesting user owns the todo before applying updates.

The request must include at least one field to update. All fields are optional but the payload must specify a minimum of one field to change.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate authentication - extract user_id from access_token in Authorization header
2. Query multi_user_todo_todos by todo_id and verify multi_user_todo_member_id matches authenticated user_id
3. Validate that request body contains at least one field to update (title, description, start_date, or due_date)
4. Validate field constraints:
   - title: max 255 characters if provided
   - description: max 10000 characters if provided
   - start_date: valid ISO 8601 datetime if provided
   - due_date: valid ISO 8601 datetime if provided
5. Build UPDATE statement with only the provided fields
6. After successful update, query the old todo values from a previous edit record (most recent edited_at) to create history entry
7. Insert record into multi_user_todo_todos_edits with old values (from previous edit or current state before update) and new values (from request)
8. Query the updated todo with all fields
9. Return 200 OK with complete todo object
10. Return 404 Not Found if todo doesn't exist or doesn't belong to user
11. Return 400 Bad Request if no fields provided or validation fails

responseBody.description: The complete updated todo record with all current field values.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the todo to update. Must belong to the authenticated user.
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Partial update object containing any combination of fields to modify. At least one field must be specified.

operations.description:
Retrieve full details of a specific todo by ID.

This endpoint returns the complete todo object including title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and timestamps. The operation validates that the requesting user owns the todo and returns 404 if the todo doesn't exist or doesn't belong to the user.

Only authenticated users can access their own todos. The system enforces data isolation by verifying ownership before returning the todo details.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_todos table by id (UUID).

Prerequisites:
1. Extract user_id from JWT access_token in Authorization header

Query logic:
- SELECT * FROM multi_user_todo_todos WHERE id = {todoId} AND multi_user_todo_member_id = {user_id}
- Return single todo record if found

Error handling:
- Return 404 if no todo found with matching id and user_id

Response contains all fields from database schema:
- id, multi_user_todo_member_id, title, description (nullable), start_date (nullable), due_date (nullable), is_complete, is_deleted, deleted_at (nullable), created_at, updated_at

Do NOT include any user-specific data beyond what's in the todos table.
Ownership validation is enforced through the WHERE clause.

responseBody.description: Complete todo object with all fields including title, description, dates, completion status, and timestamps.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to retrieve.
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Soft delete a todo by moving it to trash.

Moves the specified todo to the trash by setting is_deleted=true and deleted_at to the current timestamp. The todo is not permanently removed and can be restored from trash using the restore endpoint.

Only the owner of a todo can delete it. The system validates that the todo exists, belongs to the authenticated user, and is not already deleted before performing the operation.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the request and extract user_id from JWT token in Authorization header
2. Query multi_user_todo_todos WHERE id = {todoId} AND multi_user_todo_member_id = {user_id} AND is_deleted = false
3. If no todo found, return 404 Not Found
4. Update the todo: set is_deleted = true, deleted_at = current_timestamp
5. Return the updated todo with is_deleted=true and deleted_at set in response body

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the todo to delete
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete edit history for a specific todo.

Returns all modification records for the referenced todo, including changes to title, description, start_date, and due_date fields. Each history entry shows the old and new values for modified fields.

The edit history is sorted from most recent to oldest edits. Users can only view edit history for todos they own - cross-user access is not permitted.

If the referenced todo does not exist or has no edit history, an empty array is returned.
operations.name: history
operations.specification:
Retrieve edit history entries from multi_user_todo_todos_edits table where todo_id matches the path parameter.

1. Validate todo_id is a valid UUID format
2. Verify the todo exists and belongs to the authenticated user
3. Query multi_user_todo_todos_edits filtered by todo_id, ordered by edited_at DESC
4. For each edit record, return all edit history fields (edited_at, old_* and new_* fields)
5. Return empty array if no edit history exists for the todo
6. Handle 404 if todo does not exist or doesn't belong to user

Do NOT create edit history entry on this GET operation.
Only successful edits committed to the todo have history entries.

responseBody.description: Array of edit history entries showing all modifications made to the todo, sorted from most recent to oldest. Each entry includes the edited_at timestamp and old/new values for modified fields.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the todo to retrieve edit history for.
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
List user's deleted todos in trash with pagination, filtering, and sorting options.

Returns a paginated list of todos that have been soft-deleted and moved to trash. Each user can only view their own trash. The list includes basic todo information (id, title, completion status, dates) optimized for list display.

Users can paginate through their trash, filter by completion status, and sort by various date fields. Deleted todos retain all their data and edit history but are excluded from the normal todo list until restored.

This endpoint supports cursor-based pagination for efficient handling of large result sets. Sorting is applied after filtering, with null values (missing dates) sorted to the end.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query multi_user_todo_todos table filtering where is_deleted=true and multi_user_todo_member_id matches the authenticated user's ID.

Apply pagination parameters (page, limit) to cursor or offset-based pagination returning paginated results with total count.

Apply optional filtering on is_complete status when status parameter is provided (complete/incomplete).

Apply optional sorting by created_at, start_date, or due_date field. When sorting by date fields, null values must appear at the end of the result set.

Sort order defaults to descending for created_at (newest first), ascending for start_date/due_date (earliest due first).

Return only summary fields optimized for list display: id, title, is_complete, start_date, due_date, created_at, deleted_at.

Include pagination metadata: total_count, page, limit, total_pages.

Validate that the authenticated user has permission (always true since filtering by user ID).

Return 200 OK with paginated results and metadata. Handle empty trash gracefully with empty array and zero counts.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of deleted todo summaries optimized for trash list display.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for trash todos including pagination, filtering, and sorting parameters.

operations.description:
Restores a todo from trash back to the active todo list with all original properties intact.

This operation reverses a soft deletion by clearing the deleted_at timestamp and setting is_deleted to false. The todo returns to the normal todo list with its original title, description, dates, completion status, and edit history preserved.

Authentication is required to ensure users can only restore their own deleted todos. The operation validates that the todo exists, belongs to the authenticated user, and is currently in the trash (is_deleted=true) before performing restoration.

Errors are returned if the todo is not in trash (already active), the todo does not exist, or the todo belongs to another user.
operations.name: restore
operations.specification:
Restore a todo from trash to active list.

1. Validate authentication - extract user_id from access_token in Authorization header
2. Query multi_user_todo_todos by id = todoId AND is_deleted = true
3. Verify the todo's multi_user_todo_member_id matches authenticated user_id
   - Return 404 Not Found if todo not found
   - Return 404 Not Found if belongs to another user (do not reveal existence)
4. Check if is_deleted is actually true
   - Return 400 Bad Request with error message if already active (not in trash)
5. Perform update:
   - Set is_deleted = false
   - Set deleted_at = null
   - Update updated_at to current timestamp
6. Return the full updated todo object

Error responses:
- 400 Bad Request: todo is already active (is_deleted=false)
- 404 Not Found: todo does not exist or does not belong to authenticated user

responseBody.description: The restored todo object with all properties including id, title, description, start_date, due_date, is_complete, and timestamps.

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the todo to restore from trash
parameters.name: todoId

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo from the user's trash, removing all associated data including edit history.

This operation performs a complete removal of the todo and all its edit history entries from the system. Unlike soft delete (which moves todos to trash), permanent deletion cannot be undone. The todo's complete edit history is cascade deleted along with the todo itself.

Authentication is required. The todo must belong to the authenticated user and must be in the trash (is_deleted=true) before permanent deletion. Attempting to permanently delete an active (non-trashed) todo will fail with an error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate authentication - require valid access_token, extract user_id from JWT token
2. Query multi_user_todo_todos for todo with id = todoId AND multi_user_todo_member_id = user_id
3. Validate todo exists and is_deleted = true (must be in trash)
4. If todo doesn't exist or is not in trash, return 404 Not Found with appropriate error
5. Begin database transaction
6. Delete all multi_user_todo_todos_edits records where todo_id = todoId (cascade delete)
7. Delete the todo record from multi_user_todo_todos
8. Commit transaction
9. Return 200 OK with success message

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found: Todo doesn't exist or doesn't belong to user, or todo is not in trash
- 401 Unauthorized: Missing or invalid access_token
- 500 Internal Server Error: Transaction failure

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the todo to permanently delete from trash
parameters.name: todoId

Timestamp when the guest account was created.

ISO 8601 formatted datetime with timezone information. Represents the exact moment when this guest session was initiated and the account was registered in the system.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Session creation timestamp from multi_user_todo_guests.created_at column. ISO 8601 timestamp with timezone. Captures when the guest account was first created.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last update to this guest account.

ISO 8601 formatted datetime with timezone. Automatically updated whenever any field of the guest record is modified. Useful for determining session recency and last activity.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Last update timestamp from multi_user_todo_guests.updated_at column. ISO 8601 timestamp with timezone. Updated automatically on every modification to the guest record.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted.

ISO 8601 formatted datetime. Null when the account is active or expired. Non-null when the account has been deleted (soft delete), making it inaccessible for new sessions but preserved for audit purposes.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Soft delete timestamp from multi_user_todo_guests.deleted_at column. Nullable ISO 8601 timestamp. When not null, indicates the guest account has been soft deleted and is no longer accessible.

Total number of sessions associated with this guest account.

A computed aggregation that counts all sessions (active and expired) linked to this guest account across multi_user_todo_guest_sessions table. Useful for monitoring device usage patterns and detecting suspicious multiple concurrent sessions.
sessions_count.x-autobe-specification: Computed field: COUNT of multi_user_todo_guest_sessions records where guest_id equals the id field. Aggregation performed by the service layer. Provides total number of active and expired sessions associated with this guest.

token.x-autobe-specification: Authorization token comes from the session table.

IMultiUserTodoGuest.IAuthorized.description:
Authorization response containing guest identity and JWT tokens.

This schema represents the API response returned after successful guest account creation or token refresh. It provides the complete authentication context needed for subsequent API requests.

The id field contains the guest's UUID identity embedded in the JWT token. The fingerprint_hash uniquely identifies the guest across sessions. Token information includes access token (for API authentication), refresh token (for token renewal), and expiration times. Access tokens are used for authenticating API requests in the Authorization header. Refresh tokens can be exchanged for new access tokens without re-authenticating.
IMultiUserTodoGuest.IAuthorized.x-autobe-specification: Response object for guest authentication. JWT tokens are generated by the authentication service. The id field (guest UUID) and fingerprint_hash are embedded in the JWT token payload from multi_user_todo_guests table. Token access and refresh are JWT strings. token.expired_at is the validity timestamp (1 hour from creation for guests). sessions_count is a COUNT aggregation of multi_user_todo_guest_sessions. This schema represents a computed response object, not a direct table mapping.

id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from multi_user_todo_member_sessions.id (UUID primary key).

Client IP address when the session was created.

Used for security auditing and detecting suspicious login activity from different locations. Stored as an IPv4 or IPv6 address string.

Provides context about which page the member was viewing when the session token was generated or last used. Stored as a string path.

HTTP Referrer header value when the session was created.

Indicates which page or external site the member came from when logging in or creating the session. Helps trace user journey and login sources.

Timestamp when the session was first created.

Records the exact moment the member logged in and the session token was issued. Used for session age calculations and activity auditing.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session expires and becomes invalid.

Used for automatic session cleanup and security. Sessions must be refreshed or re-authenticated before this time. After expiration, the session token is no longer valid.

IMultiUserTodoMemberSession.ISummary.description:
Session summary record containing session identifier, client context, and lifecycle timestamps for security auditing and session management.

This type is used in paginated list responses to display sessions without nested compositions. It includes the member reference as a summary object to identify the session owner, along with client context (IP address, last visited URL, referrer) and session validity timestamps.
IMultiUserTodoMemberSession.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from multi_user_todo_member_sessions: id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at. Relation: member as $ref to IMultiUserTodoMember.ISummary (belongs-to relation). Excluded: multi_user_todo_member_id (FK column exposed as member relation object).

page.description:
Page number for pagination, 1-indexed.

Indicates which page of results to return. Page numbering starts from 1 (not 0). Used with limit parameter to control result set pagination.

Controls the size of each page in paginated results. Must be between 1 and 100. Default is 20 items per page.

created_at_gte.description:

Includes only sessions created on or after this timestamp. Use with created_at_lte to define a date range. ISO 8601 date-time format required.

Filter sessions by creation date (on or before).

Filter sessions by expiration status.

- 'active': Sessions that have not expired yet

IMultiUserTodoMemberSession.IRequest.description:
Request body for filtering and paginating member sessions.

This schema defines the search criteria and pagination options for querying member authentication sessions. All properties are computed filter parameters that control how the session list is filtered, sorted, and paginated.

Pagination controls the size and position of the result set. Filtering allows targeting sessions by date ranges, expiration status, IP address patterns, or member identity. Sorting enables chronological or status-based ordering of results.
IMultiUserTodoMemberSession.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Request DTO for filtering and paginating member sessions. All properties are query parameters, not direct database mappings. 

Pagination: page (1-indexed min 1), limit (1-100).
Filtering: Date ranges (created_at_gte/lte, expired_at_gte/lte date-time), status enum (active/expired/all), member_id uuid filter, ip LIKE pattern.
Sorting: sort_by enum (created_at/expired_at/ip), sort_order enum (asc/desc).

Query logic: Apply filters to multi_user_todo_member_sessions table, join with multi_user_todo_members if needed for display, return paginated results.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this password reset token record.

A UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) that serves as the primary key for the password reset token. This identifier is used to retrieve, reference, and audit individual token records in the database.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from multi_user_todo_member_password_resets.id (UUID primary key).

memberId.description:
Unique identifier for the member account associated with this password reset token.

A UUID foreign key referencing the multi_user_todo_members table. Links this password reset token to a specific member account that requested the password reset.
memberId.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from multi_user_todo_member_password_resets.member_id (UUID foreign key to multi_user_todo_members.id).

memberEmail.description:
Email address of the member account associated with this password reset token.

Retrieved via JOIN with multi_user_todo_members table using member_id foreign key. This email address identifies which member account the password reset token is intended for, without exposing other member profile details.
memberEmail.x-autobe-specification: JOIN from multi_user_todo_member_password_resets.member_id to multi_user_todo_members.id, returning member.email. This provides the member's email address associated with this password reset token.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this password reset token was initially created.

An ISO 8601 formatted date-time value that records when the password reset token was generated and sent to the member's email address. This timestamp is critical for tracking token age and verifying token lifetime compliance.

expiredAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this password reset token expires and becomes invalid.

An ISO 8601 formatted date-time value that marks the end of the token's validity period. Once the current time exceeds this timestamp, the token cannot be used for password reset regardless of whether it has been used. Typical token lifetimes range from 1 to 24 hours depending on security policy.

isExpired.description:
Indicates whether this password reset token has expired based on current time.

Computed by comparing the expired_at timestamp with the current time. Returns true if expired_at is in the past, false otherwise. This field enables administrators to quickly identify expired tokens without manual calculation.
isExpired.x-autobe-specification: Computed: expiredAt > current_time. Returns boolean true if the token's expired_at timestamp is less than the current datetime, false otherwise.

isValid.description:
Indicates whether this password reset token is still valid and available for use.

Computed based on token existence in the database. Tokens are immediately deleted (cascaded) when used for a password reset, so a token's existence in the database indicates it has not yet been used. Returns true if the token exists and is accessible, false if already used or deleted.
isValid.x-autobe-specification: Computed: token exists in database. Returns boolean true if the password reset token record is present in multi_user_todo_member_password_resets table (not yet used/deleted), false if already used (tokens are cascaded when used).

timeUntilExpirationSeconds.description:
Remaining time until the password reset token expires, expressed in seconds.

An integer value representing the number of seconds between the current time and the expired_at timestamp. Positive values indicate time remaining, zero indicates immediate expiration, and negative values indicate how many seconds past expiration the token has been. This field provides administrators with precise token lifecycle timing without manual calculation.
timeUntilExpirationSeconds.x-autobe-specification: Computed: expiredAt - current_time, converted to integer seconds. Returns positive value for tokens not yet expired, zero for tokens expiring immediately, and negative value for already expired tokens.

IMultiUserTodoMemberPasswordReset.IAdmin.description:
Password reset token metadata for administrative review and auditing purposes.

This response provides comprehensive token information including creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, associated member account details, and current token status indicators. The actual reset token value is deliberately excluded from this endpoint for security reasons to prevent token exposure through administrative queries.

## Computed Status Fields

The response includes three computed status indicators that help administrators assess token validity:

- **isExpired**: A boolean indicating whether the current time has passed the token's expiration timestamp
- **isValid**: A boolean confirming the token still exists in the database (tokens are cascaded/deleted when used for password reset)
- **timeUntilExpirationSeconds**: An integer representing remaining seconds until expiration, or negative value if already expired

## Use Cases

This endpoint serves administrative functions including security compliance auditing, password reset troubleshooting for support teams, monitoring token usage patterns, and support investigations requiring token status verification.
IMultiUserTodoMemberPasswordReset.IAdmin.x-autobe-specification: Fields: id, memberId, memberEmail, createdAt, expiredAt, isExpired, isValid, timeUntilExpirationSeconds. JOIN with multi_user_todo_members on member_id foreign key to fetch member email. Computed: isExpired (expiredAt > now), isValid (token exists/not used since tokens are cascaded when used), timeUntilExpirationSeconds (expiredAt - now in seconds as integer). Security: actual token value never exposed.

instruction:
# Multi-User Todo Application E2E Test Suite

## Test Scenarios

### Authentication Tests
1. User signup with valid email and password
2. User signup with duplicate email (should fail)
3. User signup with invalid email format (should fail)
4. User signup with password less than 8 characters (should fail)
5. User login with valid credentials
6. User login with invalid credentials (should fail)
7. User login with non-existent user (should fail)
8. Change password with correct current password
9. Change password with incorrect current password (should fail)
10. Change password with new password less than 8 characters (should fail)
11. Delete user account with all associated data removed
12. Access protected endpoint without authentication (should fail)
13. Access protected endpoint with invalid token (should fail)

### User Profile Tests
1. Get current user profile
2. Update user display name
3. Update display name with empty value (should fail)
4. Update display name exceeding 100 characters (should fail)

### Todo Creation Tests
1. Create todo with all fields
2. Create todo with only required title field
3. Create todo with invalid title (empty, too long)
4. Create todo with invalid dates (wrong format)

### Todo Listing Tests
1. List todos with default pagination
2. List todos with custom page and limit
3. List todos filtered by status: all
4. List todos filtered by status: complete
5. List todos filtered by status: incomplete
6. List todos sorted by created_at descending
7. List todos sorted by created_at ascending
8. List todos sorted by start_date (existing dates first)
9. List todos sorted by start_date (missing dates at end)
10. List todos sorted by due_date (existing dates first)
11. List todos sorted by due_date (missing dates at end)
12. List todos with all combined filters and sorts

### Todo Retrieval Tests
1. Get single todo by ID (exists and belongs to user)
2. Get single todo by ID (doesn't exist - 404)
3. Get single todo by ID (belongs to different user - 404)

### Todo Completion Tests
1. Mark todo as complete
2. Mark complete todo as incomplete
3. Toggle completion status multiple times

### Todo Editing Tests
1. Edit todo title only
2. Edit todo description only
3. Edit todo start_date only
4. Edit todo due_date only
5. Edit todo with multiple fields
6. Edit todo with no changes (should fail - at least one field required)
7. Edit non-existent todo (should fail - 404)
8. Edit todo belonging to different user (should fail - 404)

### Edit History Tests
1. Create multiple edits on a todo
2. Verify edit history contains all changes
3. Verify edit history sorted by most recent first
4. Verify edit history entry format (all fields present)
5. Verify edit history for todo with no edits (empty array)
6. Edit history is deleted when todo is permanently deleted

### Todo Deletion Tests (Soft Delete)
1. Soft delete a todo (move to trash)
2. Soft delete already deleted todo (should fail)
3. Verify deleted todo doesn't appear in normal todo list
4. Verify deleted todo still accessible via GET by ID before permanent delete

### Trash Tests
1. Get trash list (empty initially)
2. Get trash list with deleted todos
3. Get trash list with pagination
4. Restore todo from trash
5. Verify restored todo appears in normal todo list
6. Restore already restored todo (should fail)
7. Restore todo belonging to different user (should fail)

### Permanent Deletion Tests
1. Permanently delete todo from trash
2. Verify todo no longer appears in trash
3. Verify todo no longer accessible via GET (404)
4. Verify todo's edit history is deleted
5. Verify permanent deletion of non-existent todo (should fail)

### Privacy and Security Tests
1. User cannot see another user's todos
2. User cannot access another user's profile
3. User cannot access another user's edit history
4. User cannot restore another user's todo from trash
5. User cannot delete another user's todo from trash
6. All protected endpoints require valid authentication

### Data Integrity Tests
1. Delete user account - all user's todos permanently deleted
2. Delete user account - all user's edit history permanently deleted
3. Soft delete user's todos - count matches in trash
4. Restore todos - count updates correctly in both lists
5. Permanent delete - edit history also deleted
6. Concurrent access to same todo from different sessions (race conditions)

### Edge Cases
1. Create todo with very long title (255 characters - max)
2. Create todo with empty description
3. Create todo with future start_date and due_date
4. Create todo with past start_date and due_date
5. Create todo with start_date after due_date
6. Pagination with empty results
7. Pagination beyond total pages
8. Maximum limit value (100 items per page)
9. Very large description text (10000 characters - max)
10. Special characters in title and description
