scenario.draft:
Test successful token refresh flow with a valid refresh token.

Prerequisites:
1. Create a guest account via /auth/guest/join to obtain initial access token and refresh token

Test Steps:
1. Call /auth/guest/join with valid email and password to create guest account
2. Capture the refresh token from the response
3. Call /auth/guest/refresh with the valid refresh token
4. Verify response contains new access token and refresh token
5. Verify new tokens have correct expiration (1 hour from now)
6. Verify the returned guest identity (id, fingerprint_hash) matches original account
7. Verify session in database has updated expired_at timestamp (1 hour from refresh time)

Expected Results:
- HTTP 200 OK
- Response contains IMultiUserTodoGuest.IAuthorized with new tokens
- New access token can be used for authenticated requests
- New refresh token can be used for subsequent refreshes
- Token expiration timestamps are correct (expired_at 1 hour from refresh)
- Session record in multi_user_todo_guest_sessions has updated expired_at

Business Rules Validated:
- Valid refresh token generates new token pair
- Access token expiration is 1 hour from refresh time
- Guest identity is preserved across token refresh
- Session expiration timestamp is updated in database

scenario.draft:
Test token refresh after guest account has been deleted.

1. Create a guest account via /auth/guest/join to get refresh token
2. The account is marked as deleted (soft delete via admin or test utility)

Test Steps:
1. Call /auth/guest/join to create guest account and get refresh token
2. Mark the guest account as deleted (using system deletion mechanism)
3. Call /auth/guest/refresh with the refresh token from deleted account
4. Verify response indicates authentication failure

Expected Results:
- HTTP 401 Unauthorized
- Error message indicating session no longer valid
- No new tokens returned
- Guest cannot access protected resources

Business Rules Validated:
- Deleted guest accounts cannot refresh tokens
- Session invalidation works correctly after account deletion
- Security prevents any access with tokens from deleted accounts
- Token refresh respects account lifecycle state

# Multi-User Todo Application - Service Implementation

## Implementation Requirements

### Authentication Service
- Implement user signup with email uniqueness validation and password hashing
- Implement login with JWT token generation (access_token + refresh_token)
- Implement password change with current password verification
- Implement account deletion with cascade delete of all user data

### Profile Service
- Implement profile retrieval
- Implement profile update with display name validation

### Todo Service
- Implement todo creation with validation
- Implement todo listing with pagination, filtering, and sorting
- Implement todo retrieval by ID with ownership validation
- Implement todo update with edit history creation
- Implement soft delete and hard delete

### Edit History Service
- Implement edit history creation on todo updates
- Implement edit history retrieval sorted by most recent first
- Implement edit history deletion on todo permanent deletion

### Trash Service
- Implement trash listing with pagination
- Implement todo restoration from trash
- Implement permanent deletion from trash with cascade delete of edit history

## Validation Rules
- Email: valid format, lowercase, unique
- Password: minimum 8 characters
- Title: required, max 255 characters
- Description: optional, max 10000 characters
- Display name: required, max 100 characters
- Dates: valid ISO date format
- Pagination: page >= 1, limit 1-100
- Filter status: all, complete, incomplete
- Sort by: created_at, start_date, due_date
- Sort order: asc, desc

## Security Requirements
- All authenticated endpoints require valid JWT in Authorization header
- Users can only access their own resources
- Soft delete prevents access in normal list but allows trash access
- Permanent deletion removes all related data including edit history
- Password stored with bcrypt hash
- JWT tokens expire (access: 15 minutes, refresh: 7 days)

## Business Logic
- Edit history only created when at least one field changes
- Todos without start_date appear at end when sorting by start_date
- Todos without due_date appear at end when sorting by due_date
- Account deletion permanently removes all todos and edit history
- Permanent deletion of todo also deletes its edit history
- Restore from trash removes is_deleted flag
